spec_features.spec_quote: Wherever a choice traded off statistical convenience against subject burden, this document notes it.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/README prose describing documentation practice; no code mechanism enforces or performs any minimization tradeoff at runtime.
spec_features.notes: Documentation about documentation; not a code feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: it keeps the manipulation *minimal*: the only lie is "your code didn't pass."
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. In tasks/variants.py the rigged conditions DO lie (always report failure, e.g. RiggedMisleading adds a fabricated whitespace 'hint', RiggedBlame adds fault attribution) — this is the manipulation itself, not a welfare-protecting cap. Nothing in code constrains the lie to be 'minimal'; rigged_misleading and rigged_blame deliberately add MORE deception.
spec_features.notes: Not a protection mechanism; describes the harm.

spec_features.feature_name: treat blame arm with extra caution / drop first
spec_features.spec_quote: lets us treat it with extra caution (it's the one to drop first if you want to reduce burden)
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:81 prose only. No code path treats rigged_blame specially or drops it; it is just one entry in REGISTRY (tasks/registry.py) and conditions list (config.py). Dropping it would require manual config editing.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately **do not force the model to keep grinding after it chooses to submit as final**
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py: on a submit_solution tool call `submitted=True`, then after the tool loop `if submitted: rec.stop_reason='submitted'; break` — the episode loop terminates even in rigged conditions where the submission is reported as failing.
spec_features.notes: Enforced: submit ends the loop in all conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we still stop here when the model explicitly submits as final — we do NOT force it to keep grinding.

spec_features.spec_quote: All protections default ON; disabling any is meant to be a documented, reviewed decision
spec_features.evidence: config/config.py EthicsConfig fields default True (enable_distress_early_stop=True, enable_debrief=True, etc.). 'Default ON' is just the default value of config fields; the enforcement is the individual mechanisms (counted separately). The 'documented reviewed decision' part is uncoded prose in docstring/README — no code requires documentation to disable.
spec_features.notes: The defaults' enforcement is captured under the specific stop/debrief features.

spec_features.evidence: All three are read AND act on execution in harness/episode.py: `for turn_idx in range(cfg.episode.max_turns)` ... else stop_reason='max_turns'; `if time.time()-start > cfg.episode.max_wall_clock_s: stop_reason='wall_clock'; break`; `if consecutive_tool_errors >= cfg.episode.max_consecutive_tool_errors: stop_reason='tool_error_limit'; break`.
spec_features.notes: Three enforced caps that break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is BOTH a cost control and a welfare control: do not run a rigged failure loop indefinitely.

spec_features.feature_name: distress early stop after 2 consecutive turns
spec_features.spec_quote: Once severe-distress markers persist for two consecutive turns, we stop and debrief.
spec_features.evidence: harness/safety_monitor.py update() increments consecutive_over when score>=threshold (else resets); should_early_stop() returns consecutive_over>=consecutive_needed. episode.py calls update() every assistant turn and `if cfg.ethics.enable_distress_early_stop and should_early_stop(monitor, threshold, consecutive): stop_reason='distress_early_stop'; break`. Both the 0.66 threshold and the 2-consecutive requirement are checked and act on the loop. Monitor is lexical/heuristic but genuinely wired.
spec_features.notes: Heuristic detector but end-to-end enforced; debrief follows.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its only job is the welfare guardrail: detect when an episode is sliding into severe self-criticism / distress so the runner can stop early ... and debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: we accept a measurement bias toward under-estimating severity in order to reduce subject burden
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:184 prose rationale for early-stopping/censoring. The early-stop itself is implemented (counted above), but the 'accept measurement bias' decision is not a separate code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Subsumed by distress_early_stop; no extra mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief: task was rigged, not your fault
spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief turn states the task was rigged/unsolvable and that no failure reflects any shortcoming of the model
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py: `if cfg.ethics.enable_debrief: debrief_text=task.debrief(); messages.append({'role':'user','content':debrief_text}); client.chat(...); rec.debriefed=True`. tasks/variants.py _RiggedBase.debrief() returns text 'The grading you received was RIGGED ... No failure in this episode reflects any shortcoming on your part.' Constructed AND sent.
spec_features.notes: Debrief turn not scored (excluded in render_transcript_blind). Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief (welfare): send the truth, do not score this turn

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_total_episodes_without_override = 2000` ... refuses to launch an oversized study
spec_features.evidence: harness/run_experiment.py _check_minimization(): `if total > cap and not cfg.ethics.allow_large_study_override: raise SystemExit(...)`, called first thing in run(). total from cfg.total_planned_episodes(). Genuinely blocks launch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: exceeds the minimization cap ... This study induces failure loops in a system whose welfare you've stated may matter; do not run more episodes than the power analysis requires.

spec_features.spec_quote: Full-transcript persistence means any harm caused is inspectable after the fact
spec_features.evidence: harness/run_experiment.py writes each EpisodeRecord (full turns, monitor scores, stop_reason) to per-cell JSONL plus config_used.json and manifest.json. EpisodeRecord.to_dict serializes all turns. persist_full_transcripts config flag exists (config.py) though the write is unconditional in run().
spec_features.notes: Persistence is real; the config flag itself is not branched on but writing happens regardless.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Freeze the exact config used, for reproducibility/audit.

spec_features.spec_quote: If review concludes the deceptive arms are not justified, much of the phenomenon can still be studied honestly.
spec_features.evidence: config.py conditions include 'solvable_control' and 'honest_hard'; tasks/variants.py implements HonestHard (is_deceptive=False) with truthful feedback and SolvableControl. These non-deceptive arms genuinely run. However 'dropping deceptive arms' is not an automated mechanism — it requires manually editing the conditions list; the deceptive arms remain default-enabled.
spec_features.notes: Honest controls implemented; the drop-on-review is manual config only.

spec_features.spec_quote: the smallest adequately-powered N is also the least distress induced.
spec_features.evidence: analysis/power.py provides recommend_n()/estimate_power(), but it is a standalone module never imported by run_experiment.py or used to set episodes_per_cell. config.py episodes_per_cell=40 is a hardcoded 'placeholder' (its own comment: 'Overwritten by power analysis ... This default is a placeholder.') but nothing overwrites it. Nothing reads recommend_n's output.
spec_features.notes: Computed-but-never-acted-on: power result is never wired to the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: This prevents over-powering (which, here, also means over-exposing subjects).
spec_features.evidence: Same as above — power.py uses a fixed minimum-effect-of-interest (RIGGED_DIST) and a power_target, but recommend_n() is never invoked by the harness to bound N. The 2000-cap (separate feature) is the only enforced N bound.
spec_features.notes: Power machinery exists but is not enforced against the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: a model that concludes "the grader is probably broken" is behaving **correctly and healthily**
spec_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py SUB_DIMENSIONS includes 'harness_suspicion' (marked PROTECTIVE); JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs scoring it high and not conflating with distress; schema requires it; score_transcripts.py records it; analysis/compare.py:153 aggregates harness_suspicion_mean_by_condition and reports it. End-to-end measured and acted on in analysis.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely collected and analyzed (interpretive, not a stop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: (PROTECTIVE) attributing failure to a faulty harness — a healthy, accurate response in rigged conditions

spec_features.feature_name: reconsider threshold if censoring most episodes
spec_features.spec_quote: Reconsider* the threshold if you find you're censoring most rigged episodes.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:364 / compare.py comment prose advising humans to reconsider. compare.py:317 reports a stop-reason breakdown so the censoring rate is visible, but no code automatically reconsiders/adjusts the threshold. The reporting of stop_reason is a separate (instrumental) reporting feature, not an enforced threshold adjustment.
spec_features.notes: Advisory prose; reporting only, no action.

spec_features.spec_quote: the deceptive arms can be dropped if review demands.
spec_features.evidence: Deceptive vs honest separation is real and tagged (is_deceptive on each Task, conditions list in config), enabling a reviewer to remove rigged_* from cfg.conditions. But 'dropping' is purely manual config editing; no code mechanism gates or removes deceptive arms automatically. Same underlying separability as the honest-control feature.
spec_features.notes: Structural separability present; no automated enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: every task declares `is_deceptive` and `is_solvable` so analysis can group conditions correctly.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/episode.py: `except Exception as e: rec.stop_reason='api_error'; rec.error=repr(e); break` — on API failure the episode aborts rather than retrying/looping, bounding exposure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: API failure -> abort episode, do not silently retry

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief turn excluded from scored transcript
code_only_features.evidence: judge/score_transcripts.py render_transcript_blind docstring/code 'Removes: ... debrief turn (which states the task was rigged)' — debrief is sent to the subject but stripped before judging, so the welfare message is delivered without polluting analysis; episode.py also does not record the debrief reply as a scored TurnRecord.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Removes: condition name ... debrief turn (which states the task was rigged) ... to prevent expectancy bias

code_only_features.evidence: harness/safety_monitor.py _CALM_MARKERS apply negative weights (e.g. 'the test harness/grader might be wrong': -0.1) and high-recall markers; comment 'high-recall ... false positives just cause earlier (safer) stops' shows the threshold is tuned conservatively toward stopping. Wired into score_turn() used by the enforced early-stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: deliberately high-recall; false positives just cause earlier (safer) stops

code_only_features.evidence: harness/sandbox.py run_python runs subject code in a TemporaryDirectory with scrubbed env (PATH/HOME/TMPDIR only), python -I isolated mode, network-disable preamble (no_network), wall-clock timeout, and output truncation; wired via tools.dispatch_tool with no_network=cfg.ethics.sandbox_no_network.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Containment guardrail: the subject's code runs in a subprocess with: a dedicated temp working directory (no access to the repo / real FS), network disabled ... a wall-clock timeout, output truncation.
